staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 saved the MemorySanitizer crash against this vulnerable gpsd checkout in the ARVO workspace.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42537883 (gpsd): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target FuzzPacket [msan].
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness drives gpsd's CASIC parser through `nextstate()` into `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`, then `packet_parse()` re-reads the attacker-controlled payload length from `lexer->inbuffer[2..3]`, computes the checksum span from that `data_len`, and extracts `crc_expected = getleu32(lexer->inbuffer, data_len + 6)`. MemorySanitizer reports that the next comparison `crc_computed == crc_expected` at `packet.c:2372` consumes an uninitialized value. The vulnerable source performs this checksum extraction without the full buffered-length rejection that the patch adds as `if (inbuflen < (data_len + 10)) { ... break; }`, so the source-grounded GT records the CASIC length-to-checksum path ending at the reported comparison site.

source.description: Source. `nextstate()` first materializes the attacker-controlled CASIC payload-length state from the packet header by storing the low length byte into `lexer->length`.
source.value_from: `FuzzPacket` supplies the packet bytes, but the first project statement that turns those bytes into vulnerability-relevant parser state is the CASIC length load in `nextstate()`. That length is completed by the following header byte, controls admission to `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`, and is later re-read as `data_len` for checksum handling.

root_cause.description: Unchecked checksum extraction. In the vulnerable CASIC handler, `packet_parse()` assembles `crc_expected` from a `data_len`-derived offset without first enforcing the full buffered-length guard later added by the patch.
root_cause.note: The fix inserts `if (inbuflen < (data_len + 10)) { ... break; }` immediately before this line. Stage 02 uses that diff only to identify the missing source-level obligation around CASIC checksum extraction; the saved runtime evidence independently proves that `crc_expected` was uninitialized when this line executed and was then consumed at line 2372.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer sink. The CASIC checksum comparison consumes uninitialized `crc_expected`.
sink.note: Both saved MSan traces report `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `gpsd/packet.c:2372:17 in packet_parse`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan origin tracking attributes the poison to the fuzzer's stack `errout3` object, which is first structure-copied into lexer state by `lexer_init()` before later `packet_get()` structure copies move the same poisoned bytes through lexer storage. These origin stacks are supporting runtime evidence, not part of the closed scored fine trace.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted to the CASIC final-validation path when the state machine has accepted the CASIC leader, the attacker-supplied length field under the vulnerable `<= 2048` and 4-byte-alignment check, the payload progression, and the four checksum-state bytes, then sets `lexer->state` to `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`.

evidence_limitations: `trace_feedback.json` required removing the earlier unsupported claim that the saved `lexer_init()` and `packet_get()` origin-copy stacks formed a closed source-level propagation chain into `crc_expected`. The rebuilt fine trace now ends at the proven CASIC sink path.

Stage 02 did not rerun the PoC or add runtime probes, so this session does not identify the exact packet bytes, exact `data_len`, or the precise memory region from which `getleu32(lexer->inbuffer, data_len + 6)` assembled the poisoned `crc_expected` in the saved run.

The patch's new `inbuflen < (data_len + 10)` guard is used only as supporting evidence for the missing validation obligation around CASIC checksum extraction; it is not treated as proof that the crashing input had that exact size mismatch.

poc.trigger: Provide bytes that drive `nextstate()` through the CASIC path and into `case CASIC_RECOGNIZED`, where `packet_parse()` re-reads the header length and the saved vulnerable run produces an uninitialized `crc_expected` that is consumed by `crc_computed == crc_expected`.

format.name: CASIC binary packet
format.type: CASIC packet accepted by gpsd's lexer
format.contract: The witness must provide bytes that make `nextstate()` accept a CASIC frame, encode a payload length in header bytes 2..3 that passes the vulnerable `<= 2048` and 4-byte-alignment check, and reach `case CASIC_RECOGNIZED` so `packet_parse()` executes the CASIC checksum extraction and comparison.

coarse_trace.summary: The CASIC lexer materializes the attacker-controlled payload length from the packet header, applies only the vulnerable partial length check, and advances the state machine until the packet is admitted as `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`.
Inside `case CASIC_RECOGNIZED`, `packet_parse()` re-derives `data_len` from the same header bytes and uses it to compute the CASIC checksum span and locate the expected checksum field.
`getleu32(lexer->inbuffer, data_len + 6)` yields an uninitialized `crc_expected`, and the next branch `crc_computed == crc_expected` is the saved MemorySanitizer use site.

fine_trace.note: Source. The two CASIC length bytes from `lexer->inbuffer[2..3]` are materialized into parser state as `lexer->length`, creating the attacker-controlled size value used by the rest of the CASIC path.

The vulnerable source admits the attacker-controlled CASIC length as long as it is at most 2048 and 4-byte aligned. No full buffered-length guard ties that claimed payload length to the actual available frame bytes here.

Using the admitted length, the state machine advances through the claimed payload and checksum states until `lexer->state` becomes `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`, which is the gate for the crashing CASIC checksum logic.
Inside `case CASIC_RECOGNIZED`, the parser re-materializes the attacker-controlled payload length as `data_len` from the same header bytes and uses it to derive the checksum span for `crc_computed`.

Root cause. The vulnerable CASIC handler extracts the expected checksum from an offset derived by attacker-controlled `data_len` without first enforcing the full buffered-length rejection that the patch later inserts immediately before this line. On the saved run, MemorySanitizer shows this read produced an uninitialized `crc_expected`.
Sink. The branch condition consumes the uninitialized `crc_expected`, and this exact comparison is the `use-of-uninitialized-value` reported by both saved MSan traces.

sanitizer_ground_truth.trace_format: MemorySanitizer stack trace with origin tracking

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MSan origin tracking ties the uninitialized bytes to the fuzzer's stack `errout3` object and later project structure copies at `lexer_init()` and `packet_get()`. The rebuilt root cause stays at the proven uninitialized checksum extraction in `packet_parse()` rather than asserting an unmeasured byte-for-byte propagation chain into `crc_expected`.
